record.reference: Shepherd of Hermas — Vision 3, section xiii

source.text: Τῇ δὲ τρίτῃ ὁράσει εἶδες αὐτὴν νεωτέραν καὶ καλὴν καὶ ἱλαράν, καὶ καλὴν τὴν μορφὴν αὐτῆς· 2. ὡς ἐὰν γάρ τινι λυπουμένῳ ἔλθῃ ἀγγελία ἀγαθή τις, εὐθὺς ἐπελάθετο τῶν προτέρων λυπῶν καὶ οὐδὲν ἄλλο προσδέχεται εἰ μὴ τὴν ἀγγελίαν ἣν ἤκουσεν, καὶ ἰσχυροποιεῖται λοιπὸν εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ἀνανεοῦται αὐτοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα διὰ τὴν χαρὰν ἣν ἔλαβεν· οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀνανέωσιν εἰλήφατε τῶν πνευμάτων ὑμῶν ἰδόντες ταῦτα τὰ ἀγαθά. 3. καὶ ὅτι ἐπὶ συμψελίου εἶδες καθημένην, ἰσχυρὰ ἡ θέσις· ὅτι τέσσαρας πόδας ἔχει τὸ συμψέλιον καὶ ἰσχυρῶς ἕστηκεν· καὶ γὰρ ὁ κόσμος διὰ τεσσάρων στοιχείων κρατεῖται. 4. οἱ οὖν μετανοήσαντες ὁλοτελῶς νέοι ἔσονται καὶ τεθεμελιωμένοι, οἱ ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας μετανοήσαντες. ἀπέχεις ὁλοτελῆ τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν· μηκέτι μηδὲν αἰτήσεις περὶ ἀποκαλύψεως, ἐάν τι δὲ δέῃ, ἀποκαλυφθήσεταί σοι.
source.label: Vision 3, section xiii

translation.text:
But in the third vision you saw her younger[a], beautiful, and cheerful, and her appearance was beautiful.

For just as when some good message comes to someone who is grieving, he immediately forgets his former sorrows and accepts nothing else except the message that he heard, and from then on he is strengthened for the good, and his spirit is renewed because of the joy that he received, so also you have received a renewal of your spirits by seeing these good things.

And because you saw her sitting on a stool, the position is firm; because the bench has four feet and stands firmly. For indeed the world is held together by four elements.

Therefore those who have repented[f] completely will be new and firmly founded, those who have repented from their whole heart. You have the revelation complete. No longer ask anything about revelation; but if anything is needed[e][d][c][b], it will be revealed to you.

footnotes.text: The phrase 'good message' translates ἀγγελία ἀγαθή, which can also mean 'good news' or 'good tidings.'
'Stool' renders συμψέλιον, a small four-legged seat; 'bench' is another possibility.
'Four elements' reflects ancient cosmology (earth, water, air, fire), used here to symbolize firmness and order.
'Will be new' translates νέοι ἔσονται; it could also be read 'will be young.' 'New' aligns with the renewal imagery in this context.
'You have the revelation in full' reflects the idiomatic sense of ἀπέχεις as 'to have in full' (commercial idiom), not 'to be far from.'

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

Refers to outward look rather than metaphysical 'form'; 'appearance' is clear and natural.
Captures the ongoing experience of sorrow in an English participial form.
Avoids importing later technical sense of 'Gospel' while conveying positive report.
Common adverb of immediacy; idiomatic modern English.
Aorist of ἐπιλανθάνομαι; 'forgot' is the straightforward equivalent.
Genitive of the earlier afflictions; 'former sorrows' is concise and natural.
In context after hearing the message, the sense is taking in / embracing nothing else; 'accepts' captures this succinctly.
Causative/passive sense of being made strong; preserves the moral strengthening idea.
Prepositional phrase marking direction/purpose; 'for the good' is concise.
Standard rendering of renewal language; keeps the spiritual/moral nuance.
Abstract noun matching the verb 'renew'; consistent with the previous clause.
Retains the plural as in Greek, respecting Hermas' idiom for the inner life of multiple persons.
Context mentions four legs and standing firm; 'stool' best fits a four-legged small seat.
Focuses on the firmness of the seating/setting as explanation of the symbol.
In a cosmological statement about elements, 'world' is idiomatic while retaining scope.
Transmits the idea of being kept in its state by something; 'held together' suits the four-element motif.
Refers to the classical four elements (earth, water, air, fire) in ancient cosmology.

alternative_readings: rendered as a collective singular: 'renewal of your spirit'
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas addresses multiple hearers; the plural fits the addressees and preserves the idiom of individual inner life in each person without harmonizing to later theological usage.

theological_decisions.issue: 'The world is held together by four elements'
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Rendered literally, acknowledging ancient four-element cosmology as Hermas' illustrative framework.
theological_decisions.rationale: Maintains the symbolic explanation of the four-legged seat; translation should not modernize or correct the ancient cosmology that the text itself uses.

theological_decisions.issue: "You have the revelation in full; ask nothing further"
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Understood as closure of this revelatory sequence for Hermas, not as a universal cessation claim.
theological_decisions.rationale: The command governs Hermas' immediate inquiry about this vision; the following clause ('if anything is needed, it will be revealed to you') leaves room for subsequent necessary disclosures.

review_passes.summary: The draft is exceptionally accurate and captures the author's intent, register, and vocabulary very well. I made one minor adjustment to restore the repetition of 'beautiful' (καλὴν) in the first sentence, which the draft had varied with 'lovely'. Otherwise, the translation is excellent.
issues_found: Minor stylistic variation: The Greek repeats καλὴν ('beautiful') to describe both the woman and her appearance. The draft varied this with 'lovely', but preserving the repetition is slightly more faithful to the author's phrasing.

translation.text: For just as when some good message comes to someone who is grieving, he immediately forgets his former sorrows and welcomes nothing else except the message that he heard, and from then on he is strengthened for what is good, and his spirit is renewed because of the joy that he received, so also you have received a renewal of your spirits by seeing these good things.

base_translation.text: For just as when some good message comes to someone who is grieving, he immediately forgets his former sorrows and welcomes nothing else except the message that he heard, and from then on he is strengthened for what is good, and his spirit is renewed because of the joy that he received, so also you have received a renewal of your spirits by seeing these good things.

translation.text: Suppose a grieving person receives good news. He quickly forgets his earlier sorrows and welcomes only the message he has heard. From then on, he is strengthened for what is good, and the joy he received renews his spirit. In the same way, seeing these good things has renewed your spirits.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: For just as when some good message comes to someone who is grieving
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Suppose a grieving person receives good news.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The comparison begins with a grieving person receiving an encouraging message.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The long opening clause becomes a direct, natural setup.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: welcomes nothing else except the message that he heard
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: welcomes only the message he has heard
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The grieving person exclusively welcomes the good message.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This preserves the image of welcome rather than changing it to mental preoccupation.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: his spirit is renewed because of the joy that he received
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: the joy he received renews his spirit
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The received joy is the cause of his inner renewal.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The causal relationship is recast in a shorter active sentence.

risk_flags.risk: “Strengthened for what is good” remains somewhat broad in English.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording preserves POB’s scope without narrowing it to moral action.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: Suppose someone is grieving and receives good news. He quickly forgets his earlier sorrow and can think of nothing but the news he has heard. From then on, the joy he received strengthens him to do what is good and renews his spirit. In the same way, seeing these good things has renewed your spirits.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft substantially improves readability and rightly preserves the comparison, the joy, and the renewal. However, two simplifications recast the analogy beyond what POB states: exclusive welcoming becomes cognitive fixation, and strengthening “for what is good” becomes explicitly doing good. The recommended wording remains natural while retaining the stated images and scope.

base_translation.text: And because you saw her sitting on a bench, the position is firm; because the bench has four feet and stands firmly. For indeed the world is held together by four elements.

translation.text: You saw her sitting on a bench, showing that her position is secure. A bench has four legs and stands firmly. In the same way, the world is held together by four elements.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: because you saw her sitting on a bench, the position is firm
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: You saw her sitting on a bench, showing that her position is secure
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Her seated position signifies the firmness and security of her position.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation, immediate symbolic explanation, and grounding review
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Showing that” preserves the bench as evidence of security rather than its cause.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: because the bench has four feet and stands firmly
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: A bench has four legs and stands firmly
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The bench’s four supports explain its stability.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Modern English normally calls a bench’s supports legs rather than feet.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: For indeed the world is held together by four elements
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: In the same way, the world is held together by four elements
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The bench’s fourfold stability is compared with the world’s four elements.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB connective logic and immediate context
simplification_decisions.rationale: The explicit comparison makes the connection between the two fourfold images clear.

interpretive_expansions.claim: The world’s four elements form a symbolic comparison with the bench’s four legs.
evidence: The bench’s four legs are linked to its firmness.
The next sentence describes four elements holding the world together.
alternatives_preserved: The statement may also serve as the underlying explanation for the symbol.

risk_flags.risk: “Four elements” may be unfamiliar to modern readers.
risk_flags.mitigation: The historical expression is retained because it is essential to the fourfold comparison.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: You saw her sitting on a bench because her position is secure. A bench has four legs and stands firmly. In the same way, the world is held together by four elements.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft usefully modernizes “feet” to “legs” and makes the fourfold comparison explicit; that comparison is well supported by the immediate sequence. However, the first sentence changes the logic by making her secure position the reason she was seen sitting. Recast her sitting as the sign that shows the position’s security.
